audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL logic (EVM precompiles ecrecover/MODEXP/bn128 pairing, contract deployment collision detection, RPC interfaces, transaction processing, gas/mana metering) and CL logic (attestation inclusion windows, gossip propagation, fork activation signals).

out_of_scope: Execution Layer internals from CL perspective

el_vectors.threat: Submit malformed transactions, craft malicious precompile inputs, resource exhaustion via large MODEXP operands, phishing via wallet_watchAsset with deceptive token metadata, batch transaction abuse via wallet_sendCalls
Craft inputs to exploit edge cases in ecrecover (signature malleability), MODEXP (memory exhaustion via large operands), bn128 pairing (subgroup attacks), or CREATE2 address collision attacks
Send invalid blocks with incorrect baseFee fields, exploit Prague fork activation edge cases

cl_vectors.threat: Submit stale attestations to exploit extended inclusion window (EIP-7045), flood gossip with attestations at epoch boundaries, propose blocks with manipulated attestation sets
Provide incorrect fork activation data, censorship

misclassified_entities.reason: EXT-ATTACKER is a threat actor archetype used for illustration in EIP-684 security model, not a distinct external interface. The actual external entity is the deployer (EXT-DEPLOYER) which may be malicious.

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp via Wallet RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: DApps interact via unauthenticated wallet RPC. All request parameters (batch calls, flow control, token metadata, image URLs) are attacker-controlled. Phishing, SSRF, and resource exhaustion attacks are possible.

trusted_external_entities.name: Client via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: eth_getBlockByNumber RPC, eth_estimateMana RPC, eth_manaPrice RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Public JSON-RPC endpoint, no authentication required. Clients can query arbitrary block numbers, submit estimation requests. Block number parameters and transaction parameters must be validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Contract/EOA via EVM CALL to Precompiles
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any contract or EOA can invoke precompiles with arbitrary calldata. Input validation is critical: ecrecover must validate v/r/s ranges, MODEXP must handle zero-length and oversized operands, bn128 pairing must verify point encoding and subgroup membership. Gas metering is the primary DoS defense.

trusted_external_entities.name: Contract Deployer via CREATE/CREATE2
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: CREATE opcode, CREATE2 opcode, contract creation transaction
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any account can initiate contract deployment. EIP-684 collision detection must prevent deployment at addresses with existing nonce or code. Address collision attacks (especially via CREATE2 with pre-computed salts) must be blocked.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Engine API (fork activation signals, block processing triggers)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Authenticated via JWT between CL and EL clients. The channel is trusted for authentication, but payload content (block data, fork activation parameters) must still be validated by the EL. Incorrect fork activation could cause consensus failures.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC Transaction Submission
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users submit raw transactions via public RPC. Transaction parsing, signature validation, gas requirements, and all field validations must be performed. Malformed transactions must be rejected before state modification.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer via P2P (Block Propagation)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peer nodes propagate blocks over unauthenticated P2P network. Block headers, transaction lists, and state roots must all be fully validated. Peers may send invalid blocks, attempt eclipse attacks, or exploit fork transition edge cases.

trusted_external_entities.name: Attesting Validator via P2P Gossip
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validators submit attestations over unauthenticated P2P gossip. Attestation slot, target epoch, and inclusion window must be validated per EIP-7045 extended rules. Stale attestations must be rejected. Validators may attempt to flood the network with attestations at epoch boundaries.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Proposer via P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block proposers include attestations in beacon blocks. Proposers may selectively include/exclude attestations or include invalid ones. All attestations within proposed blocks must be validated independently.

trusted_external_entities.name: Gossip Network Peer via P2P
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P gossip channels (attestation subnet, aggregate subnet)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peers propagate attestations and aggregates over gossip. Extended gossip window conditions (EIP-7045) must be checked before propagating. Stale or malformed attestations must be dropped to prevent resource exhaustion.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full validation of batch call parameters, flow control settings (atomicity, onFailure modes), schema validation, capability scope verification, and rollback-atomicity conflict detection required.

Token type validation, address checksum verification, chain ID validation, blocked asset list check, URI scheme whitelist enforcement (https/ipfs/data only), SSRF prevention (no localhost/internal targets), phishing detection via token name similarity, and anti-fingerprinting (return before user interaction) required.
Block number parameter parsing and validation required. Fork-aware baseFee field inclusion/exclusion based on EIP-1559 activation block. Non-existent block handling.
Transaction parameter validation for estimation requests. Rate limiting recommended for public endpoints.

Validate v in {27, 28}, validate 0 < r < SECP256K1N, validate 0 < s < SECP256K1N. Handle recovery failure gracefully (return empty, not revert). Fixed 3000 gas cost prevents DoS. Input zero-padding for short inputs.

Length field parsing with zero-padding for short inputs. Zero modulus and zero base edge cases handled. Gas cost formula (EIP-2565) must accurately reflect computation cost with minimum 200 gas floor. Memory allocation must be bounded by gas to prevent OOM.

Input length must be multiple of 192 bytes. G1 point coordinates must be < p and on curve (or zero point). G2 points must have correct order q (subgroup membership check). Gas formula 80000*k + 100000 must prevent DoS. Empty input returns 1.

Collision detection must check target address nonce > 0 OR code.length > 0 BEFORE init code execution. Collision must consume all gas and revert state changes. Balance alone at target address does not trigger collision.
Fork activation block number must be validated. Prague-specific modules must only execute after fork activation. Content validation of block payloads required despite JWT authentication.
Full transaction parsing, signature validation, gas requirement checks, and field validation required. Malformed transactions must be rejected before any state modification.
Full block header validation, transaction execution, and state root verification required. Fork-specific rules must be applied based on block number.

Attestation slot must be within extended inclusion window (until last slot of epoch N+1 per EIP-7045). Target epoch must be current or previous. Minimum slot requirement must be met. TIMELY_TARGET_FLAG set without inclusion_delay constraint.
All attestations included in proposed blocks must be independently validated. Proposer censorship or selective inclusion cannot be prevented but attestation validity must be enforced.

Extended gossip window conditions must be verified before propagation. Stale attestations (outside extended window) must be dropped. Rate limiting on gossip processing recommended to prevent resource exhaustion.
